title: On-Demand Analytics Report
text:
Why this exists
Recurring reports often accumulate manual steps, hidden decisions, and formatting work. This project explores a more explicit system: defined inputs, repeatable transformations, a consistent artifact, and clear places for analyst review.

title: On-Demand Analytics Report
text:
Current state
An initial report-generation workflow and visual artifact exist. The repository does not yet contain enough evidence to describe operational use, validation, or deployment, so those details remain intentionally provisional.

title: On-Demand Analytics Report
text:
Current hypothesis
A parameterized, on-demand workflow can reduce repetitive assembly and improve consistency, while leaving interpretation and quality review with the analyst.

title: Better analytical ideas, made tangible.
section: Faster implementation changes which ideas are feasible.
text:
Faster implementation changes which ideas are feasible.
AI-assisted development can reduce the distance between a well-reasoned concept and a working interface. That means analytical work can begin with something people can test, rather than months of specifications alone.

title: Better analytical ideas, made tangible.
text:
Structure Before Sophistication
Sophisticated-looking outputs are becoming easier to generate. Framing, definitions, assumptions, architecture, and validation are not.
Poor thinking can now be implemented faster, too. Structure is the quality-control layer: the disciplined design that makes an analytical system transparent, reproducible, maintainable, and defensible.


Clear questionsKnow what the system is meant to answer.


Defensible logicMake metrics and assumptions open to review.


Reproducible systemsBuild work that can be understood and repeated.


Honest boundariesState uncertainty and limits alongside capability.

title: Better analytical ideas, made tangible.
section: A statistician’s lab for analytical systems.
text:
A statistician’s lab for analytical systems.
CentralStatz was founded by Alex Zajichek, a statistician and data scientist in Central Wisconsin with more than a decade of experience learning, teaching, and doing data science work across tools, methods, and problem contexts.
His work is especially grounded in healthcare, where messy systems, consequential decisions, and fragile metrics make sound analytical structure essential. Through the lab, Alex explores, designs, prototypes, and evaluates systems that make complex analytical questions easier to engage with—and easier to scrutinize.

title: Hospital Readmissions Explorer
text:
Project notebook · Active development




A working exploration of how conversational interaction can make public hospital-readmissions data easier to question—and its analytical logic easier to inspect.


Ask about this project Back to active work

title: Hospital Readmissions Explorer
text:
Why this exists
Public healthcare datasets contain valuable evidence, but useful exploration often requires knowledge of the source, measures, and analytical tools. This project asks whether a carefully bounded conversational layer can lower that interaction cost without pretending the underlying complexity has disappeared.

title: Hospital Readmissions Explorer
text:
Current hypothesis
A constrained interface can shorten the path from a question to an inspectable result while keeping source data, definitions, and analytical logic visible enough to question.

title: Hospital Readmissions Explorer
text:
What the prototype demonstrates

A custom web interface for asking questions about Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program data.
A deployment path connecting a conversational interaction to analytical output.
A tangible interface that can now be evaluated instead of discussed only as a specification.

title: Hospital Readmissions Explorer
text:
AI’s role
AI-assisted implementation made it faster to connect the interface, analytical workflow, and deployment pieces. It did not define valid measures, determine appropriate interpretations, review the source data, or validate whether a response is fit for a healthcare decision.

title: Hospital Readmissions Explorer
text:
What remains expert-driven
Question framing, measure definitions, analytical constraints, evaluation, interpretation, and governance remain human responsibilities. In this context, a plausible answer is not the same as a defensible one.

title: Hospital Readmissions Explorer
text:
Latest meaningful update
A deployment pipeline and custom web interface were assembled for interactive exploration of HRRP results. The next phase is less about adding surface-level capability and more about testing the structure: which questions are supported, how results expose their basis, and where the interface should decline to answer.
